newsitem.title: USA: 3Com merger has strong break-up penalties.
newsitem.headline: 3Com merger has strong break-up penalties.

text.p: 3Com Corp said it expected the company's acquisition of U.S. Robotics Corp to close early in the northern summer and that the deal calls for either party to pay substantial penalties if it backs out.

In a telephone interview, 3Com chairman and chief executive Eric Benhamou said the merger, valued at $7.3 billion on a fully diluted basis, contains "break-up fees and strong mutual lock-up provisions" should the deal unwind.
Asked if he could quantify the break-up penalties, Benhamou answered, "No, but they are quite strong."
He reiterated earlier comments made in a conference call with financial analysts that the merger would become accretive to earnings at some point in fiscal 1998, which begins in early June.

The deal is expected to close by the end of the fiscal fourth quarter in May or the beginning of fiscal 1998. The company had said it expected to take a significant one-time charge in the quarter the deal closes.

The merger -- the largest ever in the computer network industry -- will create a company with more than $5 billion in annual revenues and more than 12,000 employees in 130 countries, U.S. Robotics and 3Com have said.

Under the terms of the deal announced after U.S. markets closed on Wednesday, each share of U.S. Robotics will be swapped for 1.75 shares of 3Com. The deal is valued at $6.6 billion based on the closing price of 3Com stock, a statement said.

However, the fully diluted value of the deal is $7.3 billion if one counts the 156 million shares of 3Com stock traded for the outstanding shares of US Robotics, plus an additional 32 million shares to cover Robotics stock options.
"Based on a total of 188 million shares that we will be issuing at today's price of 39 dollars, that comes to $7.3 billion," said Barbara Shapiro, 3Com's vice-president of corporate communications.
